summary: Quickstart template defaults can trigger 429 rate limiting for self-serve accounts (concurrency too high + insufficient backoff guidance)
description:
Issue summary
- Multiple users running the Python RAG+agent quickstart on self-serve keys are hitting HTTP 429 "rate_limit" responses shortly after startup.
- Root cause appears to be template defaults spawning too many concurrent requests (agent loop + retrieval + eval smoke run) for typical self-serve quota/rate limits, plus unclear guidance on how to tune concurrency and handle 429 with backoff.

Customer impact
- Template appears "broken" during first-run experience; users see repeated errors and incomplete responses.
- Some users interpret 429s as service instability rather than expected quota behavior.
- Support load: repeated tickets + #help threads, plus churn risk during activation funnel.

Customer report (DevFoundry)
- "Ran the RAG agent template as-is. It starts, but within 1–2 minutes most requests fail with 429. Lowering max_tokens didn’t help. We’re on free credits."

Environment
- Hosted API, prod us-east
- Template: Python RAG+agent quickstart (default settings, no explicit concurrency overrides)

Observed behavior / evidence
- 429s occur during:
  1) initial warm-up / smoke prompt loop
  2) agent tool-calling loop when tools trigger multiple model calls
  3) optional eval hook (golden prompts) when run immediately after startup

Example error snippet (customer redacted)
- HTTP 429
- Body: {"error":{"type":"rate_limit","message":"Rate limit exceeded"}}
- Response headers (sample):
  - retry-after: 2
  - x-request-id: rw_req_01HS…
  - x-rw-rate-limit-limit: (varies by tier)
  - x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0

Steps to reproduce (internal)
1) Create a new self-serve org/key with default limits.
2) Run Python RAG+agent template with default settings.
3) Hit the /chat endpoint using the built-in demo route while also running the included warm-up (or run eval script immediately after starting).
4) Observe bursts of parallel requests (>= 6–10 in flight) and 429 responses; retries (if enabled) are not consistently honoring Retry-After.

Initial hypothesis
- Template defaults assume higher throughput than typical self-serve tier.
- Concurrency is effectively multiplied by:
  - agent loop iterations
  - tool calls
  - streaming reconnect attempts
  - eval prompts run back-to-back
- Backoff guidance in README is insufficient; users retry immediately or with fixed delay, causing repeated 429s.

What we need
- Update template defaults to be "activation-safe" for self-serve (lower concurrency, softer warm-up, avoid simultaneous eval run by default).
- Ensure retry middleware respects Retry-After and uses exponential backoff + jitter.
- Update docs/troubleshooting to clearly explain 429s and what knobs to tune (concurrency, max_in_flight, eval rate, max_tokens), with copy/paste config.

Resolution criteria
- Fresh self-serve key can run the template demo route and complete a simple query without 429s under normal single-user testing.
- If 429 occurs under deliberate stress, template should:
  - surface a clear error message
  - respect Retry-After
  - degrade concurrency
  - provide actionable logs with request_id
comments: 2025-02-21 (Priya Shah, Support) — Triage: seeing multiple reports of 429s on the new quickstart. Linking Slack thread: #support ("template users seeing 429s default qps too high"). Customer is self-serve; likely expected, but defaults make it look like a product issue. Assigning to Owen for investigation; looping in Monica (DevEx) + Ibrahim (SDK).

2025-02-21 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Repro’d on a fresh self-serve key in prod us-east. Template starts 6+ concurrent calls when warm-up + demo route overlap. Observed that retries are happening but not consistently honoring Retry-After; some code paths use fixed delay. Request IDs captured; no 5xx from gateway—pure 429 rate limiting.

2025-02-22 (Monica Patel, DevEx) — Confirmed: Python template default MAX_IN_FLIGHT_REQUESTS=8 (effective higher with agent tool calls). Proposal: set default to 2, make warm-up single-threaded, and gate eval behind explicit command. Also update README troubleshooting with: (1) reduce concurrency, (2) respect Retry-After, (3) consider Dedicated for higher sustained throughput.

2025-02-23 (Ibrahim Khan, SDK TL) — SDK note: we should standardize 429 handling to prefer server-provided Retry-After and apply capped exponential backoff with jitter. The template should call the shared retry helper rather than rolling its own. This aligns with ongoing work from PR-103 but needs a small follow-up for the template path that uses streaming reconnect logic.

2025-02-24 (Owen Phillips, Support) — Sent customer workaround while fix is in progress:
- Set RWI_MAX_IN_FLIGHT=1 (or TEMPLATE_CONCURRENCY=1)
- If running eval, add delay between prompts / run separately
- Ensure 429 retry respects Retry-After; otherwise disable immediate retry to avoid thundering herd
Customer confirmed workaround reduced errors but asked for better defaults.

2025-02-25 (Sahana Iyer, CI/Build) — Added a regression check idea: in CI smoke test, assert that default config does not exceed N in-flight requests against a simulated low quota; and ensure 429 path sleeps >= Retry-After. (Follow-up task filed separately.)

2025-02-26 (Monica Patel, DevEx) — Fix merged: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-quickstarts/pull/116
Changes:
- Lower default concurrency (8 -> 2)
- Warm-up runs sequentially
- 429 handler respects Retry-After, uses exponential backoff + jitter, caps retries
- README troubleshooting updated (also referenced in PR-114 structure)
Verified locally with self-serve key: demo query completes without 429 under normal usage. Marking resolved; support to monitor new tickets for 1 week.
